The remaining risks are minor — error-state masking on the home page, briefly stale data on param navigation, and a large upstream fetch fan-out that is bounded by the in-memory cache.

review_cost.rationale: Nothing here blocks correctness or requires a rewrite; the ask list is one round: split/slim the server util, drop the redundant per-game payload, use typed returns and a real 404, and delete the dead definePageMeta. Everything else is nits.

findings.issue: getPokemonPageData fetches details for every version group and every move the Pokémon can learn, then ships the entire moveGroups blob to the client even though only one game's tables are rendered — large fan-out per first render and a bloated Nuxt payload.
findings.suggestion: Add a query-param (e.g. /api/pokemon/:name/moves?game=...) or compute the selected game server-side from the route query, so the client refetches when the Game select changes.

findings.issue: A single 489-line module owns the HTTP cache, the process-global API base and pokedex index, and the DTO builders for all four page types — the highest-change-rate file every server route depends on.
findings.suggestion: Split into pokeapi/client (fetch + cache), pokeapi/index (index build) and one small module per resource; keep the exported DTO types shared so pages can consume them.

findings.issue: Not-found is returned as data ({notFound:true}), so missing resources render a 'Not found' page with HTTP 200; no error.vue and no createError is used anywhere.
findings.suggestion: Throw createError({ statusCode: 404 }) in the Nitro handlers and render error.vue, keeping the per-page useHead title via route meta or a shared error page.

findings.issue: useFetch<any> on every page discards Nuxt's typed server-route inference, even though the server module already defines the DTO shapes.
findings.suggestion: Give the Nitro handlers explicit return types and drop <any> so useFetch infers them; at minimum import the exported types from server/utils/pokeapi.

findings.issue: If /api/pokedex fails (500/network), data is undefined and the page shows 'No Pokémon found', presenting an outage as an empty result set; status/error are never inspected anywhere.
findings.suggestion: Destructure error/status from useFetch and render an explicit error message for failed fetches; keep 'No Pokémon found' for genuine zero-match states.

findings.issue: formatValue is duplicated between the move page and MoveMethodTable, and the not-found guard plus useHead title triple is copy-pasted across four pages.
findings.suggestion: Move formatValue to a shared composable/util (Nuxt 4's shared/ directory is designed for this) and wrap the fetch + not-found + title logic in one useResourcePage composable.

findings.issue: Stat-bar scale factors 255 and 720 are magic numbers inlined in template style bindings (also 622 total), undocumented.
findings.suggestion: Hoist named constants (MAX_STAT = 255, MAX_TOTAL = 720) into the script or compute bar widths server-side in the stats DTO.

findings.issue: Empty definePageMeta({}) is dead code left in the home page.

decodeURIComponent(getRouterParam(...)) risks double-decoding params if the router already returns decoded values; harmless for this API's hyphenated ASCII names but fragile as a pattern copied into all four handlers.
findings.suggestion: Rely on getRouterParam alone, or centralise param decoding in the shared pokeapi client so the choice is made once.

summary: A spec-complete, framework-current Nuxt 4.6.3 app that follows the documented patterns for reactive-URL data fetching, Nitro routes and useHead, with clean prop-only components and tokenised CSS. The merge-blocking-adjacent asks are concentrated in one file: server/utils/pokeapi.ts is a 489-line god module that also fetches and ships every game's move tables to the client. Everything else is nits — typed returns, a real 404, and a couple of duplicated helpers — so I'd merge after one contained round of changes.
